title: Sheaf Hom out of a module of finite presentation commutes with directed colimits (Stacks 0GMV)
statement: Let $X$ be a topological space and $\mathcal O_X$ a sheaf of commutative rings on $X$. An $\mathcal O_X$-module $\mathcal G$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] is *of finite presentation* if every point of $X$ has an open neighbourhood $U$ with an exact sequence $\mathcal O_U^{\oplus m}\to\mathcal O_U^{\oplus n}\to\mathcal G|_U\to0$ of $\mathcal O_U$-modules (Stacks, Modules, Definition 01BN). Let $\mathcal G$ be of finite presentation, $I$ a directed set, $(\mathcal F_i,\varphi_{i'i})_{i\le i'}$ a system of $\mathcal O_X$-modules over $I$ with a colimit $(\mathcal F,(c_i)_i)$ in $\Mod(\mathcal O_X)$ [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. Let $\mathcal H_i=\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O_X}(\mathcal G,\mathcal F_i)$ and $\mathcal H=\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O_X}(\mathcal G,\mathcal F)$ be the sheaf Homs [def-pur-sheaf-hom] (on the site of open subsets of $X$), with the $\mathcal O_X$-linear maps $\mathcal H_i\to\mathcal H_{i'}$, $\psi\mapsto\varphi_{i'i}|_U\circ\psi$, and $\gamma_i:\mathcal H_i\to\mathcal H$, $\psi\mapsto c_i|_U\circ\psi$ (for $\psi$ a section over an open $U$), Then the system $(\mathcal H_i)$ has a colimit $(\mathcal H',(d_i)_i)$ in $\Mod(\mathcal O_X)$ (the sheafification of the sectionwise colimit, Modules 01AH (2)), and the unique $\mathcal O_X$-linear $u:\mathcal H'\to\mathcal H$ with $u\circ d_i=\gamma_i$ for all $i$ is an isomorphism.

source.place: Modules, Lemma 0GMV (lemma-hom-finite-presentation-colimit), line 3759; proof uses Modules 01AH(2),(3), Modules 01CO, and Sheaves Section 009E and Lemma 00WY

proof.text: *Step 1 (localize the finite presentation).* Colimits of sheaves of modules commute with restriction to an open subset by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-space-colimit-restriction] (Modules 01AH(2),(3)), and the sheaf Hom construction is defined by restriction to the localized ringed space [def-pur-sheaf-hom]. Therefore the assertion can be checked after restricting to an open neighbourhood on which $\mathcal G$ has a presentation $\mathcal O_X^{\oplus m}\to\mathcal O_X^{\oplus n}\to\mathcal G\to0$. Replace $X$ and all modules by these restrictions; the resulting comparison map restricts back to the original map, and isomorphisms of sheaves can be checked locally by [lem-weil-pbc-sheaf-isomorphism-local-open-cover] (Sheaves 00WY).

source.place: Modules, Lemma 0GMV proof, first paragraph: taking colimits commutes with restriction to opens, so a finite-presentation module may be treated on an open where its presentation is global; Sheaves, Section 009E

proof.text: *Step 2 (the kernel presentations).* Apply [lem-weil-pbc-sheaf-hom-finite-presentation-kernel] to the chosen presentation and each $\mathcal F_i$, and also to $\mathcal F$. This gives exact rows $0\to\mathcal H_i\to\mathcal F_i^{\oplus n}\to\mathcal F_i^{\oplus m}$ and $0\to\mathcal H\to\mathcal F^{\oplus n}\to\mathcal F^{\oplus m}$. The maps $\varphi_{i'i}$ and $c_i$ induce a commutative diagram of these rows, whose left vertical maps are the $\gamma_i$ and whose other vertical maps are the canonical maps on finite direct sums.

source.place: Modules, Lemma 0GMV proof, the global finite presentation and the exact sequence obtained from Lemma 01CO

proof.text: *Step 3 (pass to the filtered colimit).* The category of sheaves of $\mathcal O_X$-modules has the required colimits, and filtered colimits are exact, by the generic sheaf-module result [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-colimits-forgetful] (used here as a tool for the ringed-space site). Finite direct sums are finite colimits, so the colimit of the systems $(\mathcal F_i^{\oplus n})$ and $(\mathcal F_i^{\oplus m})$ identifies canonically with $\mathcal F^{\oplus n}$ and $\mathcal F^{\oplus m}$. Applying exactness to the top rows in Step 2 yields an exact sequence $0\to\varinjlim_i\mathcal H_i\to\mathcal F^{\oplus n}\to\mathcal F^{\oplus m}$. The comparison diagram has isomorphisms on the last two vertical arrows, hence its induced map on kernels is an isomorphism; this induced map is the unique $u:\mathcal H'\to\mathcal H$ compatible with the cocones. Thus $u$ is an isomorphism.
